demo:
# Result Deduplication and Merging demo: SimHash-lite clustering + canonical election.
import hashlib
def fingerprint(text):
    t="".join(text.lower().split())
    return hashlib.sha256(t.encode()).hexdigest()[:16]
HITS=[{"id":"h1","src":"mirrorA","auth":0.9,"text":"Solar sails use photon pressure."},
      {"id":"h2","src":"mirrorB","auth":0.6,"text":"solar  sails use photon pressure. "},
      {"id":"h3","src":"blog","auth":0.4,"text":"Kapton survives heat better than mylar."}]
clusters={}
for h in HITS:
    clusters.setdefault(fingerprint(h["text"]),[]).append(h)
for fp,members in clusters.items():
    canon=max(members,key=lambda m:m["auth"])
    print("cluster",fp,"canon=",canon["id"],"merged:",[m["id"] for m in members if m["id"]!=canon["id"]] or "none")

description:
Signature edition — an original Signature-authored completion, clearly labeled as Signature work and never presented as public record. Result deduplication and merging turns a messy pile of overlapping hits into one clean, traceable collection. Across federated archives the same record arrives through many doors — mirrors, reprints, translations — and naive union drowns the caller in copies. The tool fingerprints candidates, clusters near-duplicates, elects one canonical representative per cluster, and keeps the full lineage so nothing is truly lost, only tidied.

This record documents the merge reversibility approach: Keep enough metadata to un-merge a cluster if a later correction shows the merge was wrong.

Teaching ladder rank 3 (advanced): this record covers production concerns — scaling behavior, failure modes, measurement, and the operational discipline needed to run this tool across a near-boundless archive.
